en: To you, the general who fights for us, the prize of victory,
and, as one delivered from terrors, my thanksgiving,
I, your city, ascribe to you, O Mother of God;
but as you have a power none can fight against,
set me free from every kind of danger,
that I may cry to you: Hail, unwedded Bride.
An angel of the first rank
was sent from heaven
to say to the Mother of God: Hail;
and with his bodiless voice,
seeing you take a body, O Lord,
he was amazed and stood still,
crying out to her words such as these:
Hail, you through whom joy will shine out;
hail, you through whom the curse will cease.
Hail, calling back of fallen Adam;
hail, ransom of the tears of Eve.
Hail, height hard to climb for human thoughts;
hail, depth hard to look into even for the eyes of angels.
Hail, for you are the throne of the King;
hail, for you carry him who carries all things.
Hail, star that makes the sun appear;
hail, womb of the divine taking of flesh.
Hail, you through whom creation is made new;
hail, you through whom the Creator becomes a child.
Hail, unwedded Bride.
notes: The kontakion (the opening stanza) and the first of the twenty-four oikoi, whose first letters run through the Greek alphabet.
Χαῖρε, the angel’s greeting to Mary (Luke 1:28), is “rejoice” as well as “hail”.
Θεοτόκος, “she who bore God”, is given as Mother of God.
Line 1.3: “your city” is Constantinople, speaking in the first person.
